name: M.M Kovalevsky
evidence: "He studied at the Imperial Kharkov University under Dmitri Kachenovsky." Lists Sorokin among his disciples.
notes: Maksim Kovalevsky (1851-1916). Identity confirmed via Sorokin. Kachenovsky was his Kharkov undergraduate teacher, not a named doctoral supervisor. Russian magister/doktor degrees (Moscow, ~1877/1880 from memory, unverified) were earned by public defense with no formal supervisor, but I found no source that says so outright, so I did not use no_doctoral_advisor.

name: M.I. Tugan-Baranovsky
evidence: The Russian Factory in the Nineteenth Century led to "a doctorate degree from Moscow University" (1898); Master's 1894, Moscow.
notes: No supervisor named. In the Russian imperial system the degree was earned by defending a published book; it may count as no_doctoral_advisor, but I found no source stating that outright.

name: Robert Staughton Lynd
evidence: "Lynd received a Ph.D. in sociology from Columbia in 1931 using an abridged version of Middletown as his dissertation."
notes: No advisor named. Took a course with John Dewey, which does not make Dewey his advisor. Middletown was a commissioned study, not a supervised project. Possible next source: American National Biography entry.

name: Alain Girard
evidence: French demographer/sociologist (1914-1996), INED from 1946 under Sauvy and Stoetzel; Sorbonne chair of demography 1964. No doctorate details given.
notes: WARNING: Wikidata Q50308520 'Alain Girard' has P184 = Jacques Bousquet. That is a different person (not the demographer Q23010280). Do not import it. Identity is confirmed: the demographer directed Jacques Lautman's 1976 doctorat d'État. I could not find his own thesis or director.

name: Maurice Halbwachs
evidence: "Les expropriations et les prix des terrains à Paris (1860-1900): thèse pour le doctorat... Université de Paris, Faculté de droit, 1909." Letters doctorate 1912/13.
notes: Two doctorates: law (1909) and letters (La classe ouvrière et les niveaux de vie, 1912/1913). No director named in any source. French Wikipedia lists Durkheim as 'maître' (mentor), not thesis director. Candidate for no_doctoral_advisor if the reviewer accepts that old French theses had no director.

name: Georges Balandier
evidence: Two doctoral theses (Sociologie actuelle de l'Afrique noire; Sociologie des Brazzavilles noires), 1954/55; Maitron calls Gurvitch his 'maître' in sociology.
notes: Georges Gurvitch is the obvious candidate (mentor, whom he succeeded at the Sorbonne), but no source names him as thesis director. The BEROSE page (berose.fr) returned 403. Copans's 2014 biography may settle it.

name: Franklin Henry Giddings
evidence: "The College gave him an honorary Ph.D. in 1897 in recognition of the scientific contribution of his Principles of Sociology. An L.L.D. followed in 1900."
notes: The ASA bio also says honorary Ph.D. 1897. Union granted his A.B. in 1888 'as of the class of 1877' without further residence. He never earned a doctorate.

name: Alain Touraine
evidence: "La Sociologie de l'action est issue d'une thèse de doctorat écrite sous la direction de Raymond Aron."
notes: English Wikipedia's infobox gives Aron as doctoral advisor, citing this source. Defended 1964 (published 1965). The secondary thesis (La conscience ouvrière) reportedly had Labrousse and Gurvitch on the jury, per a Spanish-language tribute I did not open.

name: Tolbert Hall Kennedy
evidence: Tennessee preacher-turned-sociologist; dean of the College of Social Sciences at WSU, 1944-1965; recruited Black doctoral students.
notes: Identity is confirmed at WSU. I found no source for his own PhD institution or advisor.

name: George H. Mead
evidence: "Despite never finishing his dissertation, Mead was able to obtain a post at the University of Michigan in 1891."
notes: He never completed a doctorate (studied at Leipzig and Berlin; the Berlin dissertation was never finished). Josiah Royce is listed as his Harvard academic advisor, which is not a doctoral advisor.

name: Beatrice Webb
evidence: "From an early age Webb was self-taught"; no university degree or doctorate mentioned.
notes: Self-educated, with no earned degree. The link to Beveridge is an LSE mentoring relationship, not doctoral supervision.

name: Sydney Webb
evidence: Studied law at Birkbeck "for a degree of the University of London in his spare time"; King's College London; called to the Bar 1885.
notes: Spelling in our data is 'Sydney'; the usual spelling is Sidney Webb. No doctorate (LLB-level study and the Bar).

name: Joel B. Montague Jr.
evidence: Obituary (The Olympian, 2004): received his Ph.D. in Sociology from Michigan State University; taught sociology at Washington State from 1946.
notes: No advisor found. approx_phd_year 1917 is clearly wrong: he came to WSU in 1946 and died in 2004.

name: Jean Cazeneuve
evidence: Agrégé de philosophie, docteur en lettres; "Sa thèse de doctorat soutenue, à l'âge de 48 ans" (~1963); Sorbonne chair 1966.
notes: No director named. French Wikipedia also mentions a law doctorate from Toulouse.

name: F. Ivan Nye
evidence: Family sociologist; WSC master's 1947; built the WSU graduate program in family sociology.
notes: PhD reportedly from Michigan State around 1951 (not confirmed). The WSU and NCFR obituaries returned 403. No advisor found.

name: Guy E. Swanson
evidence: "Doctor of Philosophy, University Chicago, 1948"; Michigan faculty 1948-1969; Berkeley 1969-1995.
notes: No advisor found. The UC In Memoriam 1995 text (Calisphere) would not load.

name: Michel Maffesoli
evidence: "Thèse d'État ès lettres et sciences humaines, La dynamique sociale, sous la direction de G. Durand", defended 10 June 1978.
notes: Durand directed the 1978 thèse d'État (IdRef agrees). CONFLICT on the 1973 thèse de 3e cycle: Maffesoli's site says Durand directed both, but IdRef (idref.fr/027001067) gives Pierre Fougeyrollas for the 1973 thesis. Reviewer may want to add Fougeyrollas as the 3e-cycle director.

name: Georges Gurvitch
evidence: Settled in Berlin, "où il soutient une thèse sur Johann Gottlieb Fichte"; theses L'idée du droit social and Le temps présent... in 1932.
notes: Trained in Russia (law), then Germany; French doctorat ès lettres 1932. No director named anywhere. Leon Petrazycki is a frequently cited teacher, but I did not confirm a supervisory role.

name: Louis-Vincent Thomas
phd_institution: Université de Paris, Faculté des lettres
evidence: Les Diola: essai d'analyse fonctionnelle sur une population de Basse-Casamance: thèse... Université de Paris, Faculté des lettres (1958-59).
notes: Doctorat ès lettres. No director in the catalogue records. The thesis front matter on Gallica might name one.

name: Charles Bidwell
evidence: AB 1950, AM 1953 and PhD 1956 from Chicago; joined the UChicago faculty in 1961 after two years at Harvard (recruited by Parsons).
notes: No advisor named. Parsons recruited him after the PhD; he was not his advisor.

name: Nicholas J. Demerath
evidence: Nicholas J. Demerath (1913-1996): Tulane 1940-42; completed Harvard doctoral dissertation (Ph.D. 1942); later Washington University in St. Louis.
notes: Our record conflates father and son. The known students Blalock and Mack (UNC PhDs, early 1950s) fit the elder Demerath (1913-1996, Harvard PhD 1942, UNC faculty). The listed institution, UMass Amherst, belongs to his son N.J. Demerath III (Berkeley PhD 1964). Advisor not found either way. Penn State finding aid paraphrased from search snippet (cert error on direct fetch).

name: Barbara Heyns
evidence: Aggregator profile lists Ph.D. Sociology, University of Chicago, 1967-1971; Berkeley then NYU faculty.
notes: PhD year and institution rest on an aggregator (RocketReach), so treat as unverified. The academia.edu CV returned 403. James Coleman is a plausible guess but unconfirmed; do not use it.

name: Raymond Ledrut
evidence: "Raymond Ledrut, a soutenu deux ans plus tôt [than 1968] une thèse sous la direction de Georges Gurvitch, autre professeur à la Sorbonne."
notes: French Wikipedia: docteur ès lettres, Faculté des lettres de Paris, 1966. The thesis title differs between sources (Sociologie urbaine... vs Sens et connaissance de la ville).

name: Jacques Lautman
evidence: "Essai sur les fortunes quelconques, le logement et la spéculation immobilière / Jacques Lautman ; sous la direction de Monsieur le Professeur Alain Girard" (1976).
notes: Doctorat d'État. The ENS bio-bibliography (oralemens.ens.fr, 403 on direct fetch) also says this. This is Alain Girard the demographer, pid 908266107 in this batch. Earlier 3e-cycle thesis on employers' unions; director unknown. Quote is from search snippets; neither page opened directly.

name: Takeo Doi
evidence: 1960年に「日本語の概念による精神病理学的研究」を東京大学に提出して医学博士の学位を取得 (Igaku hakase by thesis, Tokyo, 1960).
notes: A thesis-only medical doctorate (ronbun hakase); no supervisor named. The Ezra Vogel link in our data is not doctoral (Vogel's PhD is Harvard sociology). approx_phd_year 1934 is off.
